2. The accident in the present case took place on 11.07.2018.

It is the case of the petitioner as per contents of FIR that on said date, at about 06:45 a.m., petitioner was going with his colleague to Jaipur for official work on his car Duster bearing Registration No. UP-16-AN-1931 and reached Bharat Petrol Pump, Mayur Vihar, Phase-III towards Khoda and after filling of fuel in the car, he was pumping air in the tyre in absence of any staff at Petrol Pump for the same and in the meanwhile, driver of the car bearing Registration No. UP-17-T-3853 came there while driving at a high speed and negligently and hit on the leg of the petitioner.

After the accident, he came down Vivek Gupta vs Bablu on 11 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126641172/

7. The issues are decided as follows:-
ISSUE No.1 8.
In an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and in fact is the preponderance of probabilities which is applied in civil cases.
It is also the law that the tribunal is not bound by the technical rules of evidence.
Further in holding any inquiry under section 168, The Claims Tribunal may follow such summary procedure as it thinks fit.
9. Now in this case, the petitioner Vivek Gupta is the injured and witness of the accident.
In order to establish his claim, he has examined himself as PW-2 and proved FIR which is part of DAR Ex.PW2/1, medical documents and medical bills Ex.PW2/3 & Ex.PW2/2 respectively.
He stated on oath in the affidavit about the accident and how it was caused.

He has clearly deposed that the accident was caused due to offending vehicle being driven by R1 at a very high speed, rashly and negligently and he being hit with the vehicle, while he was inflating tyres of his car at petrol pump as there was no attendant at the air pressure machine.
Hence, he has stated about the rash and negligent driving of the respondent no. 1, who was the driver of the car.
Petitioner was not cross-examined by the respondents despite opportunities given and opportunity to cross-examine him was closed on 27.03.2023.
10. After investigation, the police filed the charge-sheet against respondent no. 1 the driver of the car.
Filing of charge-sheet against the driver of offending vehicle prima-facie points to his culpability.
(New India Assurance Company Ltd vs Smt. Washeema Bano (2022) SCC OnLine All 403 and Mangla Ram vs Oriental Insurance Company Ltd (2018) 5SCC 656).

ISSUE NO.2 14.
Section 168 of the Act enjoins the Claims Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation which appears to it to be just and reasonable.
The compensation should not be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.
15. The case of Raj Kumar vs Ajay Kumar & Another (2011) 1 SCC 343, is one of the most prominent judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme Court which deals with compensation in injuries cases.

entities.text: Raj Kumar vs Ajay Kumar & Another (2011) 1 SCC 343
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was held in this case that in routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under the heads-(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure.

(ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured ,
comprising (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment and (iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries.

Where the claimant suffers a permanent disability as a result of injuries, the assessment of compensation is also to be done under the head of loss of future earnings which would depend the effect and impact of such permanent disability on the earning capacity of the injured.
The tribunal should not mechanically apply the percentage of permanent disability as the percentage of economic loss or loss of earning capacity.

What requires to be assessed by the tribunal is the effect of the permanent disability on the earning capacity of the injured after assessing the loss of earning capacity in terms of percentage of the income.
It has to be quantified in terms of money to arrive at the future loss of earnings by applying standard multiplier method.
All injuries or permanent disabilities arising from injuries do not result in loss of earning capacity.

If there is no loss of employment or earning capacity, there may not be any need to award any compensation under the head of loss of future earnings, though he may be awarded compensation under the head of loss of amenities in consequent to his injuries.
16. Now, in the present case, the injured Vivek Gupta has suffered from grievous injuries.

According to his affidavit, after the accident, petitioner was treated in Metro hospital, where his MLC was prepared.
Petitioner's right leg was totally crushed and he sustained compound grade 1 distal tibia and fibula fracture with ankle dislocation.

Considering the nature of injuries, it can be readily inferred that petitioner must have remained under considerable pain and suffering due to the accident.
Hence, I find it appropriate to grant a sum of Rs.50,000/- to the petitioner under this head.
CONVEYANCE, SPECIAL DIET & ATTENDANT CHARGES 19.

20. Though petitioner has claimed attendant expenses, no evidence has been led to show that petitioner had hired any attendant during her treatment.

It cannot be ignored that family members of petitioner must have had to render their services for providing assistance to the petitioner for her routine activities and that would definitely suffer their work/job.

For claiming compensation,
necessity of employing a professional attendant/ care taker is not required and the petitioner should be compensated for the value of services of the family members, which has been or would be necessitated by the wrong doing of the driver.

22. Petitioner has claimed that he was employed as managing director with valid technologies India Pvt. Ltd. and was getting salary of Rs.4,00,000/- per month but due to injuries faced in the accident, his future career has suffered and his working capacity is completely curtailed.

income generating impairment of its extinguishment altogether (sic).
It leads to near extinction of income generation".

The ITR Returns of petitioner are Ex.PW1/2 for the period 2016-17, 2017-18 &
2018-19.

The ITR for the assessment year 2018-19 reflects the gross total income of petitioner as Rs.46,80,196/-, the gross total income of petitioner of AY 2016-17 reflects Rs. 44,14,187/- and for the assessment year 2017-18 reflects the gross total income of petitioner as Rs.40,03,301/-.

There is no documentary evidence or testimony of expert medical witness to suggest that from the date of first admission in the hospital i.e. 11.07.2018 till the last admission on 25.07.2019, petitioner was on bed rest or indisposed to work and join his office or that he did not have the option to work from home.
However, the MLC clearly reflects that petitioner suffered from grievous injuries and puncture wound over right medial malleolus was observed by the doctor.
He sustained fracture.
It is not difficult to presume that in case of fracture he must have been disabled from work for about 3 months as this would have been the minimum time to heel his wound.
Thus, his loss of income for three months is calculated as Rs.8,69,466/-.
Therefore, I award Rs.8,69,466/- as compensation under this head.

sentences.text: The next question that remains to be decided is the compensation with respect to the disability of the petitioner.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Arising out of civil appeal No. 8918 of 2010, it was held by Hon'ble Supreme Court that :-
10.
Ascertainment of the effect of the permanent disability on the actual earning capacity involves three steps.

The Tribunal has to first ascertain what activities the claim could carry on inspite of the permanent disability and what he could not do as a result of the permanent disability (this is also relevant for awarding compensation under the head of loss of amenities of life).
The second step is to ascertain his avocation, profession and nature of work before the accident, as also his age.

The third step is to find out whether ; (i) the claimant is totally disabled from earning any kind of livelihood, or (ii) whether inspite of the permanent disability, the claimant could still effectively carry on the activities and functions, which he was earlier carrying on, or (iii) whether he was prevented or restricted from discharging his previous activities and functions, but could carry on some other or lesser scale of activities and functions so that he continues to earn or can continue to earn his livelihood.
For example, if the left hand of the claimant is amputated, the permanent physical or disablement may be around 60%.
If the claimant was a driver of a carpenter, the actual loss of earning capacity may virtually be 100%, if he is neither able to drive or do carpentry.

On the other hand, if the claimant is clerk in government service, the loss of his left hand may not result in loss of employment and he may still be continued as a clerk as he could performed his clerical functions,
in that even the loss of earnings capacity will not be 100% as in the case of a driver or carpenter nor 60% which is the actual physical disability but far less.

In fact, there may not be need to award any compensation under the head of 'Loss of future earnings', if the claimant continues in Government service, though he may be awarded compensation under the head of loss of amenities on the consequences of losing his hand....."
24. The disability certificate of Dr. Hedgwar Arogya Sansthan clearly shows that the petitioner is the case of 23% disability due fracture in relation to right lower limb.
The doctor has been examined as PW3.
He deposed that considering the nature of desk job of the petitioner which requires frequent travelling he would face some difficulty in driving four/two wheelers.
He also deposed that "There will be no problem in doing the desk job.
His ankle joint has been fused, so he will have difficulty in squatting.
He will have difficulty in running."
The petitioner has not narrated how this disability will come in way of reducing the efficiency of the work in which the petitioner is engaged.

In his affidavit, he has portrayed a dismal picture by deposing that the disability has affected his future career and further that the accident has curtailed his working capacity and his family is suffering from huge financial crisis.

It is also stated by him that the physical frame of his has been shattered and he will have to re-locate himself for his future life and his future incentives are lost and he has become very depressed and formally cut off from the rest of the world.
However, these averments of the claimants do not shed light on his functional disability and cannot be taken to mean that petitioner is unable to work as before.

There is no hint in his testimony that he was thrown out from Vivek Gupta vs Bablu on 11 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126641172/
7 the job or unable to take up any job with same or better incentives.

sentences.text: His job, as per the testimony of PW3, is desk job but PW3 has not explained regarding source of his personal knowledge regarding nature of his job.
In his testimony, PW2 has deposed that he was employed as Managing Director with valid Technologies India Pvt. Ltd.

Considering that PW2 was working as Managing Director with the company and there is nothing to reflect that the nature of his job required running,
squatting or standing for long hours and further PW3 has clearly deposed that petitioner will have no problem in doing desk job, petitioner cannot be considered to be a case having any functional disability.
Petitioner has not explained as to in what manner he shall not be able to work as per his ability and qualification.

Petitioner has not led any evidence to show what work he was doing prior to accident and what work is being done by him in the office post accident, to arrive at any conclusion that petitioner's nature of job has changed drastically to his detriment and that it is due to accident solely.

No one from his company was summoned or examined to show even ex facie that nature of job of petitioner was changed by office to his disadvantage due to any incapacity of the petitioner after the accident.
Petitioner has not filed on record his ITR returns post accident period to show that there is any reduction in his income.
It is not a categorical plea of the petitioner that he has suffered from any loss of increment or promotion on account of accident.

Even though he was deposed that his future career has suffered, he has not stated anywhere that he has lost his job or was fired from his position as Managing Director or that he is not working till date.
He has only made bald assertion regarding curtailment of his working capacity and regarding his family suffering from huge financial crisis but no documentary evidence in this regard has been led.

Hence,
in my considered view, petitioner has failed to prove any functional disability in relation to the permanent disability suffered by him and hence, he is not entitled to any compensation under this head.
My view is further forfeited with citation titled as Ramvir Singh Vs. Rajesh Kumar & Ors.

LIABILITY:
29. Now, the question arises as to which of the respondents are liable to pay the compensation amount.
As the vehicle was not insured on the date of accident, it is clear that both driver and owner of the vehicle are liable to compensate the petitioner.
Thus, the Respondent Nos. 1 & 2, being driver and owner of the offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the petitioner.

RELIEF:
30.

In view of the findings on above points, I as presiding officer of this Tribunal award a total compensation of Rs.15,39,000/- (rupees fifteen lakhs thirty nine thousand only) along with interest @ 7.5% per annum on the aforesaid award amount from the date of filing of the petition till realization to be paid by both the respondents jointly and severally.
This award is required to be deposited with this Tribunal within 30 days.

10. After investigation, the police filed the charge-sheet against respondent no. 1 the driver of the car.
Filing of charge-sheet against the driver of offending vehicle prima-facie points to his culpability.
(New India Assurance Company Ltd vs Smt. Washeema Bano (2022) SCC OnLine All 403 and Mangla Ram vs Oriental Insurance Company Ltd (2018) 5SCC 656).
If any party does not accept such charge-sheet, the burden must be on such party to adduce evidence.
If the Tribunal feels that charge-sheet is collusive, it can record that charge-sheet cannot be accepted and call upon the parties at any stage to adduce oral evidence of accident and alleged negligence.
In such cases, issue of negligence must be decided on other evidence ignoring the charge-sheet.
Vivek Gupta vs Bablu on 11 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126641172/
3 12.
In the case of Cholamandalam MS General Insurance Company Ltd vs Smt. Kamlesh and Others2009 (3) AD Delhi 310 it was held that an adverse inference can be drawn when the driver of the offending vehicle does not enter into the witness box.
The compensation should not be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.
Where the claimant suffers a permanent disability as a result of injuries, the assessment of compensation is also to be done under the head of loss of future earnings which would depend the effect and impact of such permanent disability on the earning capacity of the injured.
The tribunal should not mechanically apply the percentage of permanent disability as the percentage of economic loss or loss of earning capacity.
What requires to be assessed by the tribunal is the effect of the permanent disability on the earning capacity of the injured after assessing the loss of earning capacity in terms of percentage of the income.
It has to be quantified in terms of money to arrive at the future loss of earnings by applying standard multiplier method.
All injuries or permanent disabilities arising from injuries do not result in loss of earning capacity.
If there is no loss of employment or earning capacity, there may not be any need to award any compensation under the head of loss of future earnings, though he may be awarded compensation under the head of loss of amenities in consequent to his injuries.
16. Now, in the present case, the injured Vivek Gupta has suffered from grievous injuries.
Disability certificate was filed and relied on by the petitioner and the same reflects 23% disability in relation to right lower limb.
In view of the judgments above-said, it can be said that the respondents cannot avoid the liability cast under Statue, merely because some of the medical bills were paid for by the medi-claim policy taken by the petitioner, as the payment made under the medi-claim policy was under a contract and petitioner paid premium for the insurance policy taken by him.
It cannot be ignored that family members of petitioner must have had to render their services for providing assistance to the petitioner for her routine activities and that would definitely suffer their work/job.
For claiming compensation,
necessity of employing a professional attendant/ care taker is not required and the petitioner should be compensated for the value of services of the family members, which has been or would be necessitated by the wrong doing of the driver.
Petitioner has not led any evidence to show what work he was doing prior to accident and what work is being done by him in the office post accident, to arrive at any conclusion that petitioner's nature of job has changed drastically to his detriment and that it is due to accident solely.
No one from his company was summoned or examined to show even ex facie that nature of job of petitioner was changed by office to his disadvantage due to any incapacity of the petitioner after the accident.
It is not a categorical plea of the petitioner that he has suffered from any loss of increment or promotion on account of accident.
Hence,
in my considered view, petitioner has failed to prove any functional disability in relation to the permanent disability suffered by him and hence, he is not entitled to any compensation under this head.

28.

Therefore, he is entitled for interest @ 7.5% per annum on the aforesaid award amount from the date of filing of the petition till realization.
LIABILITY:
29. Now, the question arises as to which of the respondents are liable to pay the compensation amount.
As the vehicle was not insured on the date of accident, it is clear that both driver and owner of the vehicle are liable to compensate the petitioner.
Thus, the Respondent Nos. 1 & 2, being driver and owner of the offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the petitioner.

30.

This award is required to be deposited with this Tribunal within 30 days.
